links.targetTitle: Primitive Instances inherit a base class of operational logi

title: Agent Primitive Instances inherit operational logic from the Sky Core Atlas, and edits to the base class propagate automatically
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.5.1.2.1.2.1 uses explicitly object-oriented language: "This Instance inherits the base class of operational logic defined in [A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1 - Routine Protocol], subject to the qualifications specified in [A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.3.1 - Near-Term Process]." It then states the consequence outright: "**Modifications to the base operational logic automatically propagate to this Instance.** In future iterations of the Grove Artifact, a version of the full process definition customized to Grove will be included herein."

This is inheritance with **live binding**, not copy-paste templating. The Agent Artifact does not contain the process; it contains a pointer to it. A change at the Sky Core level takes effect in Grove without a Grove proposal, a Facilitator review, or a token holder vote.

The benefits are real: no drift between Agents, one place to fix a bug in a shared process, and no duplication across however many Agents exist. The same pattern appears in A.6.1.1.2.2.5.1.2.1.1.2, where the Instance's Tracking Methodology is a reference to a shared "Ethereum Mainnet General Tracking Methodology" rather than a Grove-specific definition.

The cost is a genuine limit on Agent sovereignty. Grove's operating rules can be rewritten by an actor Grove does not control, through a process Grove's own governance does not participate in. Combined with A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 (edits may not violate the Core Atlas), authority runs strictly downward: the parent can reach into the child, and the child cannot reach up.

The closing sentence also flags that this coupling is understood as temporary — a Grove-specific process definition is planned, which would convert live inheritance into a forked copy and change the propagation property entirely.
description: Grove's Distribution Reward Instance holds no process text of its own — it references a Sky Core Routine Protocol, so Sky can change how Grove operates without any Grove governance action.
